newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian bourse dull after strong last week.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian bourse dull after strong last week.

text.p: Shares opened dull on the Nigerian stock market on Monday following last week's robust activities, traders said.
The all-share index rose to 6958.14 from Friday's 6950.33 on sustained gains by oil, food and beverages shares but with volume low, traders said.
"Turnout of brokers was normal but the dull market only reflects the mood of the season," said one dealer.
Unlike last week when shares took big leaps, Monday's opening was sober, he added. Seventeen stocks rose and eight eased.

The most active shares remained petroleum marketers of which Mobil led with a 40 kobo rise to 49.00 naira followed by Total which rose 25 kobo to 56.80 naira. National Oil and Texaco rose 20 kobo apiece to 45.50 naira and 32.70 naira, respectively.
Nigerian Breweries touched 19.60 naira on Monday, up 30 kobo while Nestle Foods and Union Dicon Salt, leading food equities, added 10 kobo each to 47.80 naira 43.50 naira, respectively.
West African Portland Cement Company soared 60 kobo to 45.10 naira. Traders said the shares were rising against the sectoral trend because of its low price earning ratio.

Big Monday losers included tyre maker Dunlop which slid 30 kobo to 9.30 kobo. Conglomerates CFAO was down 13 kobo to 2.63 naira and UTC went two kobo lower at 90 kobo. Ashaka Cement also fell 10 kobo to 17.10 naira.
All the losses were due to large volumes flooding the market, traders said.
